target_customer: California adult cannabis consumers who pay an annual membership for discounted delivered products
problem: Legal cannabis in California was sold at high retail markups; the founders offered wholesale-style pricing through a membership and delivery.
business_model: Annual membership plus direct-to-consumer retail margin on cannabis delivery

founders.name: Ted Lichtenberger
previous_startups: Old Pal (cannabis brand, per search results)

founders.name: Scott Davies
founders.background_notes: Arcata resident and farm owner who has worked in Humboldt cannabis for three decades, per Lost Coast Outpost April 2019.

founders.name: Tony Diepenbrock
founders.background_notes: Named as founder in the April 2019 Lost Coast Outpost article; not on the YC page.

competitors.name: Eaze
competitors.what: On-demand California cannabis delivery app moving into recreational delivery
competitors.funding_then: $27M Series B in September 2017, total about $52M

technical_complexity.rationale: E-commerce and delivery logistics; the hard part was licenses, supply and compliance rather than software.

defensibility.rationale: California cannabis licensing and a vertically integrated supply give some barrier; membership gives mild stickiness, but retail was open to any licensed rival.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Eaze later shrank and cannabis delivery stayed fragmented per search results.

market_need_then: California opened recreational sales in January 2018 and legal retail prices were high relative to the illicit market; the company argued retailers charged an egregious markup (Lost Coast Outpost, April 2019).

branding.domain_note: Uses flowercompany.com; FLOWER CO. was also marketed as Wholesale Cannabis Club in a directory listing.

identity.voice_and_tone: Blunt, humorous: We sell weed on the internet

branding.brand_signature: The nickname Costco of Cannabis, from Leafly coverage, with a flat annual membership fee
branding.community_and_virality: Leafly, TechCrunch, Edge Media Network and local outlets covered the Costco of Cannabis angle in 2019.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear positioning line and plain name earned trade and press attention, but the name is generic for the category and no source shows brand-led growth.

outcome_analysis: FLOWER CO. positioned itself as a Costco of cannabis in California and moved from delivery into owning stores. Reported funding is a $16M Series A in December 2021 and roughly $19M total, which is modest, and it is listed as active with 30 people. No sale, shutdown or layoff was found, but profitability and scale are unknown.
notes: Series A $16M in December 2021 is reported by CB Insights and a yespress CEO profile (aggregator style outlets); Persana gives January 2022; no company press release found. Investors come from VC Backed (aggregator). Totals conflict ($18.9M, $19.45M, and $2.8M on Wellfound). The yespress page was blocked when fetched, so its details come from search summaries. Eaze funding is from a 2017 TechCrunch article; Eaze later rounds are not used. Company says it was founded 2018 (several sources), YC page says 2019. Headquarters conflict between Los Angeles and San Francisco.
